# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-4945

# Review — PAN-4945
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — a Settings / `pan token revoke` revocation of an OAuth token is still undone once the revoked record is pruned at expiresAt + 7 days, inside the 90-day refresh window (FR-6 / AC-5)

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4945-review-4c03b3cf
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4945/.pan/review/agent-pan-4945-review-4c03b3cf/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4945 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4945
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/4979
- HEAD reviewed: 4c03b3cf728349fc693e92fb016348b66b52d6e8
- Prior cycle: agent-pan-4945-review-1171fef8 at 1171fef8 (CHANGES REQUESTED, one blocker)
- Changes since prior cycle: `e57c8e88092` fix(dashboard): prune OAuth access tokens by expiry only; a merge of origin/main (PAN-4944: `needs-you` route, new `answer_*` MCP tools, `route-scopes.ts` row — all from main, not this PR's diff against main); workspace chore commits.

## Blocking Findings

### [correctness/security] The cycle-1 fix only moves the revocation bypass from day 7 to day ~37 — `src/lib/access-tokens.ts:518`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: specification defect, in_pr_scope; same root cause as the cycle-1 blocker. D-8.6 reads "A record that no longer exists, because it expired and was pruned, is not a revocation." A record can be both revoked and expired, and pruning it erases the revocation. Pruning by `expiresAt` only makes "missing" mean "expired", but not "expired and never revoked".
- Why the earlier review missed it: cycle 1 proposed exactly the fix that landed ("prune OAuth records by `expiresAt` only, so a missing record always means expired"), and I checked it only against the 7-day trigger. The access token lives 30 days, but the refresh token lives 90 days from the sign-in, so the record can still be pruned while the refresh token works. That recommendation was incomplete. The author implemented it correctly.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: the operator revokes the sign-in's current access token under Settings → Access Tokens (or `pan token revoke`). The record is kept until `expiresAt + 7 days`, which is at most 37 days after the last mint, and the 10-minute sweep (`agent-token-sweep.ts:94`, `AGENT_TOKEN_PRUNE_AFTER_MS = 7 days`) then removes it. The family's `refreshExpiresAt` is the sign-in time + 90 days and does not move. A refresh in that gap finds no record (`oauth-service.ts:480-484`), treats it as expired-and-pruned, and mints a new 30-day access token.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected (FR-6, AC-5, D-9, `configuration/mcp.mdx` "Revoking"): the sign-in ends at its next refresh. Observed: a client that stays idle for 5+ weeks after the revocation gets a new token with no operator involvement. An occasionally used connector is the case the 90-day refresh lifetime exists for. Settings → Access Tokens is still the only dashboard-GUI revocation path in this slice (PAN-4946 not shipped). `pan mcp oauth revoke` and `DELETE /api/mcp-oauth/sign-ins/:familyId` are unaffected.
- Evidence: runtime probe against this HEAD's source (`npx tsx`, scratchpad script, isolated temporary `OVERDECK_HOME`, injected service clock). Flow: register → authorize → approve `operate` → exchange → `revokeAccessToken(family.accessTokenId)` → clock +N days → `pruneEndedAccessTokens(7 days, now)` → `refresh`.
  - N = 8: `pruned 0`, refresh `invalid_grant` (the cycle-1 case is fixed; matches the new test at `oauth-service.test.ts:313`).
  - N = 38: `pruned 1`, refresh `true NEW ACCESS TOKEN MINTED` (the bypass is still there).
- Fix: keep the revocation fact until the family's refresh window has surely closed. Two options:
  1. **Recommended, smallest:** keep a *revoked* OAuth record until its family's refresh token can no longer work. A family is created when its first access token is minted, so `refreshExpiresAt ≤ revokedAt + 90 days`. Prune a revoked OAuth record only when `now − (revokedAt + REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_MS) > olderThanMs`. An unrevoked OAuth record keeps pruning by `expiresAt` (then "missing" really means "expired, never revoked"). The registry should take the 90-day bound as a parameter or a shared constant, not import `oauth-flow`. The extra records are bounded: rotation-revoked records stay about 3 per family.
  2. End the family at revocation time from the dashboard (an `onAccessTokensRevoked` listener that ends the family when the revoked record is its current `accessTokenId` and is not expired). This is more robust, but the listener must ignore rotation revocations and removal-as-revocation diffs (`access-tokens.ts:158`), so it is more invasive.
  Spec correction: amend FR-1 and D-8.6 to say a revoked OAuth record outlives its family's refresh window. Regression tests: the cycle-1 probe at +38 days and at +89 days must answer `invalid_grant` and leave the family revoked; also cover a revocation after one rotation (sign in, refresh once, revoke the new current token, jump to that token's `expiresAt` + 8 days, refresh → `invalid_grant`), because `refreshExpiresAt` is pinned to the original sign-in. Update the `docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md` sweep sentence to match.

## Non-blocking Findings
Carried from cycle 1, still accurate at this HEAD (no code change in those regions):
- `~` Unauthenticated `POST /oauth/mcp/register|token|revoke` buffer the full body before any size check (`routes/mcp-oauth.ts:95,134,147`); no server-wide body limit exists. LAN-only today (H-1); worth a byte cap before W-FUN1 opens Funnel.
- `?` A LAN peer can evict a real pending approval by flooding authorize (oldest of 20 dropped, `oauth-service.ts:333`); accepted hazard H-1.
- `?` (spec) OAuth access tokens are plain `kind: 'token'` records, so they also authenticate `/api/*` and `/ws/*` within their scopes; there is no `/mcp` audience binding.
- `~` `DELETE /api/mcp-oauth/sign-ins/:familyId` on a refresh-expired, unrevoked family revokes it but answers 404 (`oauth-service.ts:202`); cosmetic.
- `?` `POST /oauth/mcp/revoke` with an access token already revoked elsewhere does not end the family (`oauth-service.ts:525`); the family ends at the next refresh instead. Fixing the blocker keeps that true.
- `?` Settings → Access Tokens shows an expired, unrevoked OAuth token as active until it is pruned (the list has no expiry notion); fits PAN-4946.
- (spec) The code-exchange order checks `used` before expiry, which is intended and commented; D-7 steps 1-2 could be reworded.
- Resolved since cycle 1: the stacked `last-verified` comments in `.overdeck/context/codebase/concerns.md` are folded.

Main-merge interaction checked: PAN-4944 adds six `approve`-scoped `answer_*` MCP tools. An OAuth `approve` sign-in gains them by scope, and `read`/`message`/`operate` do not (`mcp-oauth-acceptance.test.ts` still asserts `operate` lacks `answer_permission`; it passes). This is consistent with D-3.

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** cycle-1 fix verified for its stated window; the same defect remains for a longer window (blocker).
- **Security:** this is a revocation bypass (blocker); the other cycle-1 security advisories are unchanged.
- **Performance:** no change. The recommended fix keeps a few more revoked records per family, which is bounded.
- **Requirements/UX:** see AC matrix.

## Verification
- Verification gate: `.overdeck/pipeline.jsonl` records `verification.passed` for head `4c03b3cf` at 2026-11-04T03:28:50Z.
- Focused tests at 4c03b3cf: 15 files, 164 tests passed (the 9 OAuth test files, `mcp.test.ts`, `mcp-acceptance.test.ts`, `route-scopes.test.ts`, `no-loss-matrix.test.ts`, `access-tokens.test.ts`, `access-tokens-agent.test.ts`).
- Lints: `lint:effect-diagnostics` ✓ (227 known, none new), `lint:circular` ✓, `lint:file-size` ✓, `lint:slash-commands` ✓, `lint:docs` ✓, `lint:effect-facades` ✓.
- Runtime probe (scratchpad `probe2.mts`, `npx tsx`, isolated `OVERDECK_HOME`): N=8 → `invalid_grant`; N=38 → new access token minted.
- CI on PR #4979 for 4c03b3cf: build, core/effect lint groups, test shards and e2e were pending at review time, so they are unverified. Passed: skills/state lint groups, prompt-trailer gate, clean install + server smoke, mobile-android.

## Scope Note
This is the second cycle on the same root cause. The cycle-1 recommendation was incomplete; the author implemented it exactly. The fix above also addresses the 90-day refresh window, and the regression test should cover a revocation well past `expiresAt` (for example +38 d and +89 d).
